Verdict

Reviewed 28 Oct 2026 · next 26 Jan 2027

Feature-rich AntV graph engine, MIT and capable, but 88 MB and 104 packages installed, 413 KB gzip, 333 open issues and no release in 90 days. Hold unless you specifically need its layout or analysis features.

Current Reviewed version 5.1.1 Requirement: Graph visualization in a React application

Reasoning

  1. MIT, public repository, 12.4k stars, no OSV advisories.
  2. Canvas/WebGL rendering, many layouts and graph algorithms.
  3. Very heavy: 88 MB / 104 packages and 413 KB gzip.
  4. 333 open issues and no npm release in 90 days (5.1.1 from May 2026), although commits continue.
  5. No npm provenance.

Caveats

  • The install and bundle cost is roughly 3x Cytoscape and 7x Sigma.
  • Large issue backlog; slower release cadence than the other candidates.
  • Nineteen maintainers mitigate bus factor but complicate release consistency.

Decision context

Approved

cytoscape is the primary choice for Graph visualization in a React application. This package is classified as On hold.

The NVL suite is denied: its LICENSE.txt limits use to Neo4j Aura or commercial Neo4j, it publishes no repository, carries no provenance and cannot be loaded by Node in either module system. 1.2.2 was checked separately: same licence and packaging, different layout stack, so the denial applies to both. Adopt Cytoscape.js as the primary renderer: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 138 KB gzip, and layouts via extensions. Use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper because react-cytoscapejs is stale. Adopt Sigma.js as the fallback for large graphs: MIT, WebGL, 110 KB gzip and active, but client-only (WebGL2) and without provenance; pair it with graphology and @react-sigma/core. Hold @antv/g6 (88 MB, 104 packages, 413 KB gzip, 333 open issues, no release in 90 days) and @xyflow/react (excellent node editor, but not an exploration or layout engine).
